newsitem.title: USA: Nebraska corn harvest limited by high moisture.
newsitem.headline: Nebraska corn harvest limited by high moisture.

text.p: Dry weather in Nebraska last week aided the dry-down process, but most corn remains too wet for harvest, according to the Nebraska agricultural statistics service.
Thirteen percent of the crop was harvested as of Sunday, down slightly from 14 percent last year and behind the 30 percent average pace.
The state's corn crop was rated 97 percent mature, down from 99 percent a week ago, and up from a 96 percent average pace, the state reported.
Sixty-four percent of the soybean crop was harvested, up from 22 percent a week ago and ahead of 43 percent a year ago.
Eight percent of the sorghum crop was harvested, down from 28 percent a year ago and behind the 34 percent average pace.
Ninety-eight percent of the wheat crop had been sown, up from 88 percent a week ago and 97 percent a year ago, and close to the 99 percent average pace.

Topsoil moisture was three percent very short, 16 percent short, 79 percent adequate and two percent surplus. Subsoil moisture levels were eight percent short, 88 percent adequate and four percent surplus.
